calls.title: Design System Sync
calls.summary: The team discussed ongoing efforts in migrating and developing UI components, with Omar nearing completion on link migration but facing complex cases ahead. Theresa is working on converting designs from Figma to React code, collaborating closely with Kari to find automation solutions. Johnny is in the process of developing the text field component, with plans for further assignments. The panel component is ready for development, aiming to replace legacy components during a phased rollout. Additionally, the team is standardizing text field sizes to promote uniformity and enhance user experience while addressing communication challenges linked to background noise, recommending written updates for better clarity.
calls.keywords: Design System, React Components, Figma Integration, Component Migration, Link Migration, Standardized Sizes

calls.title: Design System Sync
calls.summary: The team convened to accelerate the development of style guides aimed at ensuring UI consistency and minimizing rework. Key discussions included refining elements like helper text, selectors, and addressing existing quality issues across dropdowns, popovers, and button styles. Individuals like Johnny Martinez and Kari Kay outlined roles in creating guides and integrating design review robots to enforce component usage across the codebase. Priorities were set on components frequently misused or structurally complex, with improvements targeting onboarding and governance to streamline collaboration. The session highlighted the importance of mental health as team members balance workload pressures with product launch timelines.
calls.keywords: Design system, style guides, components, design review automation, dropdown selectors, team onboarding

calls.title: Design System Sync
calls.summary: The team convened to address critical issues regarding badge standardization and style guide development to enhance product consistency. They identified approximately 236 badge variants, many of which were duplicates, and planned to block the creation of new badges outside a standardized set. Additionally, badges, tags, and statuses were clarified to reduce confusion, and new status icon atoms were introduced for flexibility. The development of multiple UI style guides was underway, with a focus on quickly delivering essential text content for automated checks, while ensuring design components conform to updated standards. Automation processes, such as Adriel's proposed audit robot, were set to enforce design rules and flag inconsistencies. User experience considerations included managing tab limitations and enhancing navigation features.
calls.keywords: Design System, Badges, Style Guides, Avatar Component, Tabs, Automation Robot
calls.action_items:
**Kari Kay**
Clean up badge and status design system files and send the link to Adriel Vieira to enable audit automation (13:08)
Provide notes and guidance to Johnny regarding tab usage limits, sticky behavior, and persistence features to be included in the tab style guide (29:00)

**Johnny Martinez**
Continue developing and share style guides for remaining components, focusing on avatars, buttons, dropdowns, and tabs, ensuring text-focused content for robot usage without delaying on images (21:36)
Review dropdown style guide and add detailed guidance on usage rules such as delete option coloring and group label styling to prevent design drift (24:00)

**Adriel Vieira**
Prioritize audit scans for badges and statuses using the automation robot and begin automating review and prototyping enforcement upon receiving near-complete components and style guides from Kari and Johnny (32:50)

**Gabe Melean**
Coordinate with Johnny Martinez to gain access and start contributing to the style guide development process based on Johnny’s demonstration (32:44)

**Unassigned**
Plan future improvements on avatar color assignment logic to potentially remove random assignment and improve consistency (18:22)

calls.title: Design System Sync
calls.summary: The team discussed improvements to the style guide, emphasizing specific components for product alignment. Kari highlighted refining avatar guidelines, advocating for square root avatars with rounded edges and using T-shirt sizes for consistency. The badge and status components were also standardized, with efforts to reduce color overload. Dropdown styling was addressed, enforcing uppercase labels and clarifying dropdown sizes based on logical grouping. UI bugs were identified, including issues with dropdown dividers and popover behavior, with plans for fixes. The team aimed for a unified T-shirt size system for all components, including badges and buttons. Next steps focused on individual responsibilities to finalize the style guide and enhance user interface consistency.
calls.keywords: Avatar, Dropdown Menu, Popover, Style Guide, T-shirt Sizes, Badge Component
calls.action_items:

Review Avatar, button, call out, drop down menu tabs, text area, and text field components to include specifications such as initials in avatars and shape/style usage in product (00:00)
Revise style guides for dropdown menus, focusing on label casing, grouping, divider lines, dynamic menu behaviors, and hover zone and tooltip behavior issues (05:32)
Finalize and send updated style guides for dropdowns and avatars for internal review by Kari (26:08)

**Kari Kay**

Review Johnny’s submitted style guide drafts and coordinate further refinements as needed (26:08)

**Adriel Vieira**
Audit and standardize T-shirt sizing for all components to ensure consistent engineering implementation aligned with the design system (26:41)
Fix dropdown menu UI bug causing inappropriate divider lines when menu items are conditionally hidden (09:45)
Implement uppercase styling on dropdown menu labels via CSS to avoid manual updates and ensure consistency (07:07)
Adjust button sizing to correct the extra small size mapping from size one to the proper size consistent with other components (29:04)

calls.title: Design System Sync
calls.summary: The team met to discuss the need for cleanup and consistency within the design system, currently deemed 60% accurate. Key issues included incorrect button sizes, misalignment of badges and avatars, and the need for distinct checkbox spacing and font weight adjustments. Pagination problems affecting UI behavior were highlighted, particularly issues with jumping page numbers and inconsistent item counts. Prioritization strategies were discussed, focusing on impactful yet manageable fixes, especially regarding link color updates that revealed scoping challenges. Lastly, the need for better alignment between the style guide and engineering work was emphasized, alongside the importance of improving workflows for task completion across various components.
calls.keywords: design system, button sizes, checkbox groups, pagination, style guide, component cleanup

calls.summary:
# Design System Sync
Date: 2026-08-25 | Duration: 7m

## Summary
The team discussed significant worries regarding the transition to a new managed warehouse, emphasizing risks associated with losing key members and unclear contingency plans. Participants, including Adriel Vieira and Gabe Melean, noted the importance of transparency in communication, especially relating to the lack of prior discussions surrounding major changes. The design system has also faced delays due to limited bandwidth and competing priorities, with progress on essential documentation stalled. Johnny Martinez highlighted the need for incremental modernization of outdated UI components to enhance user experience without overwhelming the team. Overall, the meeting shed light on demands for clearer role definitions and improved communication to better navigate ongoing challenges.

## Keywords
managed warehouse, design system, product UI rules, component cleanup, risk management, workload bandwidth

## Action Items

**Gabe Melean**
Prepare a rough draft of the product UI rules document after reviewing existing materials to advance the design system (03:52)
Dedicate more time this week to design system efforts to advance preparation for version 1 release (03:52)

**Johnny Martinez**
Compile a list of design components perceived as outdated to plan updates aimed at making the product's appearance more contemporary (05:30)
